rooms.10704: Two stranded icebergs stand like gateposts here, their bases gnawed by the waves into dripping overhangs, and your boat rides the swell in the gap between them. North, the gap opens onto the wider grey of the Southern Ocean, while south the water runs on among scattered floes. A bank of fog sits on the water to the west, so thick and still that a boat rowed into it soon drifts back out where it began. Close beyond the bergs looms the black headland of Cape Voogk, crusted with old snow.
rooms.10714: The black cliffs of Cape Voogk rise sheer from the water close beside you, streaked white by nesting birds and glazed with ice wherever the spray can reach. A line of stranded icebergs runs away to the west, aground on some hidden shoal, and only the narrow gap to the north lets out onto the open sea. Swell rebounds off the cliff foot and slaps the hull from two sides at once. South, the water opens out among drifting floes.
rooms.10724: The point of Cape Voogk is near enough here that you can hear the sea working in its caves, a hollow boom that comes and goes with the swell. East, the water swings out around the cape itself, where a white race of current marks the turn. Rimed grey floes nudge one another in the slack water, and frost smoke curls off the open leads between them. Northward lies the gap in the stranded bergs, and the open sea runs on to the west and south.
rooms.10799: The headland of Cape Voogk ends here in a tall black crag leaning out over the water, its ledges white with frost and old birdlime. On its very top stands a cairn of stones and whale bones, raised long ago by someone who wanted this cape found again. The current races round the point and heaps up short, steep waves that toss the boat about. East lies the South-Eastern Mira Retrum, south the water rounds the foot of the cape, and west it runs back into the Southern Mira Retrum.
rooms.10530: Around the point the sea changes its temper: the water runs dark and deep, and a long, heavy swell lifts the boat and lets it down with slow patience. This side of Cape Voogk is a wall of black basalt split into tall columns, bearded with icicles where meltwater froze in mid-fall. West, the way runs back around the point, while the South-Eastern Mira Retrum stretches away east and south, grey and enormous.
rooms.10531: Under the cliffs lies a narrow beach of grey shingle, worn smooth and stained dark where seals haul out, and the wind brings their rank, fishy smell across the water. Ice has built up along the tideline in a ragged white rind. The boat wallows in the deep swell, and spray freezes in beads along the gunwale. Open water leads east along the coast, west toward the cape, and south into the wider gulf.
rooms.10532: A glacier comes down to the sea here between two shoulders of dark rock, ending in a cliff of ice as blue as deep water where it has freshly broken. Every so often something gives within it with a crack like a whip, and a slab slides into the sea with a roar. The water is thick with brash, the broken leavings of the glacier, which hiss and clink against the hull. Safer water lies south, away from the falling ice, and the coast runs on both east and west.
rooms.10533: The face of the glacier walls in the coast here, sheer and fissured, its blue depths clouded with grit and the dark shapes of stones carried down from the heights. Chunks calved from it bob in the swell, some as big as a cottage, rolling over now and then to show their sea-polished bellies. The air is sharply colder in the shadow of the ice. West, the glacier front goes on; east and south the water is clearer.
rooms.10534: A frozen waterfall hangs from the lip of the cliffs here, a great pale beard of ice where a stream once leapt into the sea, and somewhere behind it water still trickles. Below it the cliff foot hides under a heaped apron of fallen icicles. The swell runs long and smooth, and the boat climbs each grey hill of water and slides down its back. Dark cliffs march away east and west, and to the south the gulf lies open.
rooms.10535: The cliffs above are terraced with narrow ledges, every one whitened with droppings, and the stink of the rookery drifts out over the water on the cold air. A din of shrieking and squabbling rises and falls high overhead, never quite stopping. Feathers float on the black water and cling to the oars. The ledges run on along the cliffs to the east, the coast falls back toward the glacier in the west, and the deep gulf opens south.
rooms.10536: A lone sea stack stands off the cliffs here, a tower of dark rock cut away from the land by the patient sea, wearing a cap of old snow like a cowl. The swell bursts against its foot in sheets of white that freeze where they fall. Between the stack and the cliff runs a slot of black water too narrow and too wild to risk. Safer water lies east and west along the coast, and south toward the open gulf.
rooms.10537: The ribs of a wrecked ship stand up from the rocks at the cliff foot here, black and bare as the bones of some drowned beast, and a stump of mast still leans from the wreckage. Whatever she carried the sea took long ago, and ice now fills her hold to the brim. The swell sucks and gurgles among the rocks around her. You can row on along the coast either way, east or west, or stand out south into the gulf.
rooms.10538: The cliffs dwindle here into a jumble of fallen boulders furred with ice, and beyond them, far off over the land, a dark line of forest stands against the grey. When the wind comes off the shore it carries a smell of resin and wet needles, strange after so long among salt and ice. The water runs east toward that wooded shore and west beneath the cliffs, and the open gulf lies south.
rooms.10539: The gulf comes to a corner here, where the cliffs meet the shore of the forest, and a reef of black rocks, awash and boiling white, keeps any boat from the land. Beyond the reef a dark cave mouth opens at the foot of the cliffs, giving out a low moan each time the swell runs into it. The water lies open only to the south and back west along the coast.
rooms.10549: The shore of the Great Forest of MiNar lies close here, a pale strand beneath overhanging cliffs with dark firs crowding the heights above, but a line of breakers keeps you off. Whole trees stripped grey by the sea lie tangled in the shallows beyond the surf. North, the water runs toward the reef at the gulf's corner, and south it follows the shore, while to the west the deep gulf spreads out under a low sky.
rooms.10559: The swell rears up green over a shoal here and breaks white across hidden rocks between you and the land, flinging spray that rattles on the boat like thrown gravel. Beyond the surf, under a long lip of overhanging cliff, a shadowed strand follows the coast, and above it the forest stands dark and silent. North and south the water runs beside the breakers, and west it falls away into the deep.
rooms.10569: A gap opens in the reef here, a lane of dark, quieter water where the surf cannot find its footing, and it leads east toward the very end of Mira Retrum and a landing beneath the cliffs. The smell of the forest is strong, resin and leaf mould riding on the cold. North and south the breakers run on along the shore, and west lies the open gulf.
rooms.10580: The sea ends here against a steep bank of grey shingle, where the swell runs up hissing and draws back with the rattle of a thousand stones. East, the shingle rises into the mouth of a long, low gallery that the waves have carved beneath overhanging cliffs, a dry place to drag a boat ashore. High above, the firs of the Great Forest of MiNar lean out over the edge. West, the water widens back into the gulf.
rooms.10581: You stand on dry shingle in a long gallery the sea has gnawed from the cliff foot, its roof of dark rock low enough to touch and hung with pale roots from the forest above. Grey light and the sound of surf come in from the open side, where the beach slopes west to the water's edge. North, the gallery runs on along the shore in shadow. East, a cleft in the back wall slopes out to the edge of the Great Forest of MiNar, and the smell of pine comes through it.
rooms.10588: The gallery runs on beneath the cliff, its floor a strip of cold shingle between the rock wall and the lapping edge of the sea. Driftwood lies heaped against the wall, bleached and smoothed, and roots dangle through cracks in the roof, dripping steadily onto the stones. The air is damp and smells of salt and wet earth. South, the gallery widens toward the landing; north it bends on along the shore, growing dimmer.
rooms.10589: The roof comes down low here and you must stoop, the rock above slick with seepage and crusted with salt where spray has dried. A tidal pool lies in a hollow of the floor, so clear and still that the weed and pink shells in it look painted. From somewhere ahead comes a deep, slow booming, the sea breathing in and out of a cave. North, the gallery leads on toward that sound, and south it opens back along the shore.
rooms.10590: The gallery ends in a high, echoing cave whose walls glisten with brine, and every swell that runs in through a crack in the rock fills the place with a sound like a great drum. In the middle of the floor a shaft drops down into wet, packed sand, but a fall of rock and old timber has choked it, sealing whatever lies below. The only open way is back south along the shore.
rooms.10579: Here the gulf ends in a corner between the breakers off the shore and the edge of the drift ice, a heaving white field of broken floes jammed together as far as the eye can follow. Where the two meet they grind and groan in a confusion that no boat could live through. The only clear water runs north along the shore and west beside the edge of the ice.
rooms.10578: The drift ice lies hard by, a broken plain of floes, slabs and pressure ridges that lifts and settles with the swell like the breathing of some vast sleeping thing. Its edge is a ragged line of slush and tilted plates that grind together with a sound like millstones. Frost smoke rises from the narrow strip of open water beside it. The way lies north into the gulf, or east and west along the ice.
rooms.10568: An iceberg has rolled over here, and its upturned belly rises from the sea smooth and glassy, the green-blue of old bottle glass and shot through with trapped bubbles. Water streams from its flanks in little falls, and it rocks very slowly, still finding its balance. Faintly, from the east, comes the sound of surf on the shore; north, south and west the gulf is open.
rooms.10558: A raft of drift timber floats here, whole trees washed out from the forest shore and stripped grey, bound into one tangle by ice frozen between the trunks. Weed trails beneath it, and the water around is littered with bark and needles. Beyond the surf to the east the dark forest stands under a heavy sky, and the gulf opens north, south and west.
rooms.10548: A squall of sleet hisses across the water, stinging the face and rattling on the boat, and when it passes the world comes back washed and colder. In the clear spell the coast shows plainly, cliffs falling away to the north and the dark forest rising beyond the surf to the east. The swell runs heavy and steep here. South and west, open water reaches back into the gulf.
rooms.10547: The sea here wells up from far below in slow, oily swirls that smooth the surface, colder even than the water around and smelling faintly of fish and deep places. Strands of torn weed turn lazily in the eddies. North, toward the coast, the black ribs of a wreck show against the cliffs. The gulf spreads out east, south and west.
rooms.10557: A great flat-topped iceberg towers over the boat here, its sheer white sides higher than any city wall and so long that both ends are lost in mist. The waves have cut a deep notch along its waterline, and the swell surges into the notch and booms. Cold pours off the ice like the draught from an open door. The water stays open all around its foot, and you can row on whichever way you choose.
rooms.10567: The long white flank of a flat-topped iceberg runs off into the mist to the north, and from here you can see where a slab has fallen from its corner, leaving a raw blue scar. Rubble of shattered ice still spreads over the water, clinking as it knocks together. The wind has dropped, and the stillness is so deep you can hear the ice settling. East, south and west, the gulf lies open.
rooms.10577: The wind comes howling down off the drift ice, lifting spindrift from the floes in long white streamers that hiss across the water and sting like thrown sand. Beyond the edge the ice runs on, ridged and broken, until it fades into a blur of blowing snow. The boat pitches in a short, cold chop. Shelter of a sort lies north toward the great flat-topped berg, and the floe-edge runs on east and west.
rooms.10576: A broad floe lies against the edge of the drift ice here, flat and white, and in its middle a pool of meltwater shines as blue as a stone set in a silver brooch. Its rim has rotted into a low lip of honeycombed ice that crumbles wherever the swell washes over it. North, the gulf opens deep and grey, while east and west the ragged ice-edge runs on.
rooms.10566: Two great floes have shoved together and buckled, throwing up a ridge of tilted blocks like a broken wall, each slab as thick as a man is tall and glazed green beneath. The ridge creaks and shifts as the swell works at it, and now and then a block topples into the sea with a heavy slap. Open water skirts the ridge on every side, leaving your way free in any direction.
rooms.10556: Something has killed here: a floe drifting past is stained pink and rust-red along its edge, strewn with torn scraps of blubber and a scatter of grey feathers. The water around it is very still and very dark. Faint cries carry from the bird cliffs to the north. Open water leads east toward a great flat-topped berg, and south and west into the grey.
rooms.10546: An iceberg of spires and pinnacles rises here like the ruin of some white temple, its towers leaning at odd angles and its broken arches dripping into the sea. Wind moans through its hollows in a long, low note that rises and falls. Beyond it to the north the sea stack stands against the cliffs. The water runs on clear to the east, south and west.
rooms.10545: Waves have worn a cave into the flank of an iceberg here, a smooth hollow whose light glows a deep, unearthly blue, as though the ice held a lamp somewhere inside. Water drips from its roof in a quick, ringing patter that echoes out over the swell. From the north drifts the reek of the bird cliffs, and the gulf runs on east, south and west.
rooms.10555: A pale sun shows through thin cloud, ringed by a great halo of light, with a false sun glowing at either side like two lanterns hung in the sky. The ice on every floe glitters beneath it, and the black water is laid with a bright, trembling road that gives no warmth at all. Clear water lies open on every hand.
rooms.10565: Snow falls thick and slow here, great soft flakes that drift down without a sound and vanish the moment they touch the black water. It gathers on the gunwale and on your shoulders, and it closes the world in until only a few boat-lengths of sea remain. Somewhere out in the whiteness, ice is grinding. Open water seems to run on in every direction, as far as the snow lets you see.
rooms.10575: Mist lies over the drift ice here, so that the floe-edge seems to dissolve into nothing a few yards off, and from somewhere inside the whiteness comes the sharp crack and long groan of ice breaking. Droplets bead on every rope and freeze there. The darker water of the gulf to the north is easier to trust, and the ice-edge runs on east and west.
rooms.10574: The swell runs in under the drift ice here, and the whole white field rises and falls in long, slow ripples, like a sheet shaken out by giant hands. Floes clap together as each wave passes, and slush squeezes up between them with a wet sigh. The open gulf lies north, and the edge of the ice leads on to the east and west.
rooms.10564: The clouds are low and grey, but their undersides glow a hard, bright white wherever ice lies out of sight beneath them, so that the sky itself is a map of the frozen sea. Under that pale light the water looks black as ink. A few rotten floes drift past, grey and sodden, sinking slowly into slush. Open water reaches away on every side.
rooms.10554: Growlers drift all about here, lumps of old ice no bigger than a cart, low in the water and glassy-dark, the kind a careless boat finds only by striking one. Now and then they knock against the hull with a hollow sound like knuckles on a door. The air is raw and smells of nothing but cold. Clear water leads off between them north, east, south and west.
rooms.10544: Frost smoke rises from the sea in thick, curling wisps, the water so much warmer than the bitter air that it steams like a cauldron. The vapour climbs, freezes and glitters, and hides everything beyond an oar's length. Somewhere north the frozen waterfall must still hang from its cliff, but nothing shows of it now. The open gulf runs east, south and west into the white.
rooms.10543: A dirty iceberg drifts here, banded with grey grit and stones the glacier gathered on its long way down, and a boulder as big as a hut sits on its crown as if set there on purpose. Every so often a pebble melts loose and drops into the sea with a small, neat plop. North, the glacier's face shows blue across the water, and open sea runs east, south and west.
rooms.10553: The gulf is at its widest here, a great grey bowl of water ringed with distant land: cliffs and a glacier on one hand, a dark smudge of forest on another, and the long, pale line of the Ice Wall on a third. Floes drift across it slowly, as if they had all the time in the world. The cold is steady and patient. Open water stretches away in every direction.
rooms.10563: Jade-green ice rises from the sea here in a low, heavy berg, the colour of seawater frozen from beneath rather than snow pressed from above, its flanks as smooth and glossy as polished stone. It sits so deep that the swell washes over its shoulders without stirring it. The boat feels very small beside it. The way is open on every side.
rooms.10573: Floes have been driven one over another along the edge of the drift ice here, stacked like roofing slates in a builder's yard, and the topmost plates hang out over the water with icicles dripping from their lips. The heap creaks and settles as the swell moves beneath it. Open water lies north in the gulf and runs along the ice-edge east and west.
rooms.10572: An iceberg has been caught fast in the edge of the drift ice and leans at a drunken slant, its high side white and its low side green where the sea has been at it. The floes around it are heaved and cracked from the pressure, and now and then it groans like a ship's timbers in a storm. The open gulf is north, and the ice-edge leads on east and west.
rooms.10562: A ship's boat lies locked in a floe here, frozen in up to her thwarts, her planks silvered with frost and her bow lifted as though she were still trying to climb free. No one has sat in her for many winters, and gulls have whitened her gunwale. Open water winds around the floe, leading north, east, south and west.
rooms.10552: A skin of new ice covers the sea here, thin and dark and so supple that it bends with the swell instead of breaking, rising and falling like oiled cloth. Where the bow pushes into it, it splits into long fingers that slide one over another with a faint, glassy tinkle. The cold is fierce and still. Beyond the dark sheet, open water shows north, east, south and west.
rooms.10542: Chunks calved from the glacier drift out here on the current, blue and white, some as heavy as wagons, turning slowly as they go. North, the glacier itself fills a notch in the coast, a frozen river ending in a cliff. The water is grey and stiff with slush that drags at the oars. Clearer water lies east, south and west.
rooms.10541: Pancake ice covers the water here, hundreds of round plates the size of shields, each with a raised rim where it has bumped against its neighbours, so that the sea looks paved with pale lily pads. They knock and whisper together on the swell. North, under the cliffs, the stained shingle of a seal beach shows dark. Open water runs east, south and west.
rooms.10551: An iceberg curves here in the shape of a horseshoe, its two arms enclosing a pool so calm that it mirrors the ice without a ripple. Outside the arms the swell runs on, but within there is no sound except the drip of meltwater. A boat could rest there in perfect shelter. The sea lies open beyond it, north and south, east and west.
rooms.10561: A current sets hard across the gulf here, and where it meets the swell the water stands up in short, steep ridges that never move on, breaking and re-forming in the same place over and over. The boat bucks and slews, and you must lean on the oars to hold a course. Beyond the rip, the pale cliff of the Ice Wall shows through the haze. Rough water runs on north, east, south and west.
rooms.10571: A lead of black water opens into the drift ice here, a long, narrow lane between the floes that widens and narrows as the ice breathes, tempting and treacherous. Slush clots along its edges. Nobody wise would row into it, for it can close in a heartbeat. The open gulf lies north, and the ice-edge runs on to the east and west.
rooms.10570: This is a cold corner of the gulf, where the sheer cliff of the Ice Wall comes down to meet the drift ice, and the two grind against each other with a sound like a mill that never stops. Ice dust hangs in the air and glitters. Only two ways lead out of the corner: north beside the wall, or east along the edge of the floes.
rooms.10560: The Ice Wall rises right beside the boat, and high in its face a cave opens like a round blue throat, running back into the ice farther than you can see. Meltwater drips from its lip in a steady chain of drops, each one ringing as it lands. Breath smokes in the cold that flows down out of it. North and south the water runs along the wall, and east lies the open gulf.
rooms.10550: Here the boat runs beside a cliff of ice like the side of a mountain: the Ice Wall, its face banded in layers of white and blue like a cut cake, each band a year of snow pressed hard. Thin falls of meltwater spill from ledges far up and turn to spray before they reach the sea. North, the wall runs on toward the cape; south it marches beside the water, and east the gulf lies open.
rooms.10540: The black rock of Cape Voogk gives way here to the Ice Wall, which grows from the cape's foot like a frozen buttress and runs away into the haze. Where rock and ice meet, a long crack weeps meltwater into the sea. West, the water rounds the foot of the cape; north it follows the cliffs, and to the east and south the gulf spreads wide.
rooms.10798: Here the boat rounds the foot of Cape Voogk, where the black rock plunges into the sea and the Ice Wall begins, grown onto the cape like a white rampart taller than any tower. The current pulls hard along the joint, swirling with slush. North, the water runs up to the point of the cape; east and west, the seas on either side of it open out.
rooms.10734: East, the sea swings round the foot of Cape Voogk, where the black rock of the cape vanishes beneath the first pale cliffs of the Ice Wall, and the current runs out that way in ropy, glassy swirls. On this side the water lies grey and quiet, scattered with small floes that turn as they drift. North, the point of the cape shows dark, and south and west the Southern Mira Retrum stretches away into mist.
rooms.10744: The Ice Wall rises sheer beside the boat, too high to see the top of, a cliff of blue-white ice grooved from crest to waterline by old meltwater and glazed with new. A cold draught spills down its face and across the water like air from a cellar. North, the wall bends toward the cape; south it runs on unbroken, and west the open sea lies grey.
rooms.10754: A great crack splits the Ice Wall from its crest to the sea here, a dark seam choked far back with fallen ice, and the wind sighs in and out of it like something breathing. Blocks that dropped from its lips lie half sunk in the water at its foot, slowly turning blue. The wall runs on north and south, and the sea opens west.
rooms.10764: The foot of the Ice Wall is buried here under an apron of fallen blocks, some as big as cottages, heaped where they crashed down from the face, and fresh blue scars high on the cliff show where they came from. It would be a poor place to linger when the ice is restless. North and south the water runs beside the wall; west lies open sea.
rooms.10774: The Ice Wall begins to bend away here, and south, beyond its end, two icebergs stand so close together that only a thread of dark water runs between them. The swell slackens in their shelter, and the sea turns smooth and heavy, like cold oil. North, the wall marches back toward the cape, and west the Southern Mira Retrum opens out among drifting floes.
rooms.10784: Two icebergs crowd together here, one leaning against the very end of the Ice Wall and the other grounded on the edge of the ice shelf, and between them a narrow strait runs south, scarcely wider than two boats side by side. Their flanks rise sheer and dripping, and the light between them is blue and dim. North, the water widens back along the wall; west, it runs out beside the edge of the shelf.
rooms.10785: The strait turns here between walls of ice so high and close that only a crooked ribbon of grey sky shows overhead. Every sound comes back doubled: the drip of meltwater, the knock of the oars, your own breath. The black water is perfectly still, and cold rises from it like a mist. North, the strait leads back toward open sea; east it bends on around the iceberg's foot.
rooms.10786: The strait widens at last, and the walls of ice fall back to show, south, a sheltered bay lying calm beyond the end of the Ice Wall, its shore pale with shingle and snow. Beside you the iceberg leans close, streaming with meltwater. The air is suddenly still, as though the wind could not find its way in. West, the strait winds back between the icebergs.
rooms.10787: A crescent of grey shingle curves around still water here, sheltered on every side, and over the bay the Ice Wall rises like the edge of the world, blue in its hollows and white at its crest. Moss and tufts of hardy grass grow in the lee of the stones, startlingly green, and the bleached ribs of a whale stand upright in the shingle to make an arch. No wind reaches this place, and the silence rings in your ears. North, a narrow strait leads back between two icebergs to the sea.
rooms.10783: The edge of the ice shelf runs along here as a low white cliff, flat-topped and level as a table, with the sea chewing caves into its foot. East, two icebergs crowd close together, and a narrow strait opens between them. The water is calm in the lee of the shelf and scattered with brash. North and west, the open sea stretches away among drifting floes.
rooms.10773: A slow whirlpool turns here, wide as a threshing floor, where the current curling out from the strait meets the swell, and slush rides round and round it in a lazy grey spiral. The boat swings gently with it unless you pull clear. East stands the last pale bend of the Ice Wall, and south the edge of the shelf lies low and white. North and west, the sea is open.
rooms.10763: A sheet of young ice has formed in the lee of the floes here, and on it grow frost flowers, thousands of feathery white crystals no taller than a thumb, delicate as lace and gone at a touch. They glitter like a meadow of salt in the grey light. East, the Ice Wall looms near, and north, south and west the water lies open between the floes.
rooms.10753: Meltwater pouring off the Ice Wall lies over the sea here in a cold, fresh layer, and where the oars dip they leave trails that shimmer and blur like heat over a summer road. A cupped handful tastes almost sweet. The wall itself stands close to the east, streaming with a dozen thin falls. Leads of open water wander off north, south and west between the floes.
rooms.10743: Every little while a boom like a thunderclap rolls out from the Ice Wall as some piece of its face gives way, and a moment later a long, heavy ripple arrives to lift the boat and rock it. Chips of fresh ice come bobbing out across the water, clear as glass. The wall stands to the east; north, south and west the sea lies open.
rooms.10733: An oar has been frozen upright into a floe here, its blade snapped off and its shaft wrapped in a scrap of faded red cloth, set as a marker by someone who meant to come back. Beyond the floe the black point of Cape Voogk looms close. Small floes drift past on every side, but the water stays open north, east, south and west.
rooms.10723: Somewhere among the floes, seals are barking, a hoarse, echoing chorus that carries far over the flat grey water and stops as suddenly as it began. The nearest floe is pocked with round breathing holes, their rims glazed with frozen spittle and worn smooth by whiskered snouts. North, the stranded bergs stand in a line against the sky, and the sea runs on east, south and west.
rooms.10713: The stranded bergs stand in a wall here, grounded so hard on their hidden shoal that the swell breaks against them as against a cliff, and only rubble and brash fill the gaps between. Their bases are scooped into dark, dripping overhangs. East, the line runs on toward the gap beside the cape's black cliffs; west it stretches away into the haze, and south the sea opens out.
rooms.10712: One of the stranded bergs has been worn here into a tall, thin spire, leaning out over the water like an accusing finger, and the sea has eaten so deeply into its base that it seems certain to fall. Icicles hang from its underside in a ragged fringe. The line of grounded bergs runs on east and west, and the open sea lies south.
rooms.10722: Grease ice lies thick on the water here, a soupy film of frozen crystals that takes the shine off the sea and smooths every wave, so that the surface looks dull and oily, like fat cooling in a pan. The oars slide through it with a soft hiss. North rise the stranded bergs, and east, south and west the dull water stretches on.
rooms.10732: Someone camped on a broad floe here not long ago: a windbreak of cut snow blocks still stands in a half-ring, slumping now, around a black smudge of soot and a scatter of fish bones. Tracks of boots lead to the floe's edge and stop. The open sea lies all about it, north and south, east and west.
rooms.10742: Each time the oars dip here the water flares with tiny green sparks, as if the sea were full of drowned stars, and the boat leaves a faint glowing wake that fades slowly behind. Under the low grey cloud the glow is easy to see. The sea is calm, and the boat is free to go any way at all.
rooms.10752: An iceberg drifts here veined with stripes of clear, deep blue where meltwater ran into its cracks and froze again, so that it looks like white marble shot through with sapphire. Its top is crusted with old snow that the wind has carved into sharp ridges. Open water surrounds it, running north and south, east and west.
rooms.10762: A squall of hail sweeps across the sea here, hard white pellets that bounce off the floes, rattle in the bottom of the boat and pock the water into a hissing grey froth. It passes almost as quickly as it came, leaving a thin white crust on every surface. Behind it the water lies open again to the north, east, south and west.
rooms.10772: The water here is clear enough to show a great spur of ice reaching out beneath the surface from a nearby berg, pale green and ghostly, close enough under the keel to make you hold your breath. Above the waterline the berg looks harmless, a low white hump. Open water leads away from it north, east, south and west.
rooms.10782: A long rift splits the edge of the ice shelf here, a blue chasm too narrow for any boat, its walls hung with icicles and its depths lost in shadow. The swell runs into it and comes back with a hollow sigh. The shelf's white cliff runs on east and west, and to the north the open sea is scattered with floes.
rooms.10781: The sea has gnawed a cave into the ice shelf here, a low dark mouth fringed with icicles like the teeth of some great beast, and each swell that runs into it comes out again as a deep, wet growl. Spray has frozen in fans across the shelf's white face. The shelf runs on east and west, and north lies open water.
rooms.10771: A broad floe drifts past here with the snow on its back stained a curious pink, as though someone had spilled watered wine across it, and the stain smells faintly of melon. Sailors' tales say it is a weed that grows in snow. The floe turns slowly, and open water lies beyond it on every side.
rooms.10761: Deep inside a clear-sided iceberg here a dark shape is frozen, long and coiled, too big for any fish and too long for any whale, with what might be a ridge of fins along its back. The ice around it is flawless, as if it had been sealed there on purpose. It is hard to look away. The sea is open north, east, south and west.
rooms.10751: The sea lies in a dead calm here, so smooth that every iceberg stands on its own reflection and the floes seem to hang above a second, upside-down world. The only movement is the slow ring of ripples spreading from your oars, and not a breath of wind stirs. Open water lies all around you, glassy in every direction.
rooms.10741: A thin grey drizzle falls here and freezes the moment it lands, glazing the oars, the gunwale and your sleeves in a crust of clear ice that crackles when you move. The floes are glossy with it. Through the murk to the west a low black skerry shows above the water, and the open sea runs on north, east and south.
rooms.10731: A low floe drifts here so fouled with droppings that its snow is streaked yellow and green, and the reek of it, fishy and sharp, catches in the throat. Its surface is scored with long, smooth furrows where small bodies have tobogganed on their bellies to the water's edge, over and over. Open leads run off from it every way you might want to go.
rooms.10721: The air plays tricks here: far-off icebergs seem drawn out into towers and battlements, and some float clear of the sea altogether, upside down, like castles hung from the clouds. They shimmer, shrink and grow again as you watch. Nearer at hand the water is flat and grey, and the stranded bergs stand to the north. Real open water, at least, lies on every hand.
rooms.10711: The sea has bored a hole clean through the foot of a stranded berg here, and each swell that runs into it bursts out of a vent in the ice above in a roaring spout of spray, hanging in the air a moment before it rains down glittering. The ice all around the vent is glazed and fluted. East and west the grounded bergs run on in their long line, and south the open sea is quieter.
rooms.10710: Two stranded bergs lean together here, and the gap between them is choked with a jumble of broken ice, slabs and blocks frozen into one heaving mass that groans as the swell works at it. No boat could force a way through. The line of bergs goes on east and west, and south lies the open water.
rooms.10720: A broad, low floe rides here, worn smooth and stained brown in great patches where heavy bodies lie to sleep, and tufts of coarse grey hair are frozen into the ice. The smell of seal is rank and strong, and a distant grunting and coughing carries across the floes. North stand the grounded bergs; elsewhere clear water lies all around the floe.
rooms.10730: The air itself glitters here, filled with tiny crystals of ice that drift and sparkle in the thin sunlight like dust in a sunbeam, though there is no cloud for them to fall from. They settle on your eyelashes and sting the skin. It is very still and very cold. The sea, calm and pale, lies open on every side.
rooms.10740: A long, oily swell is running here, the leavings of some storm far beyond sight, and the floes lift and settle on it in slow unison, like sleepers breathing. Each crest rolls under the boat without breaking. West, a low black skerry rises close at hand, the swell creaming white around its foot. Open water runs north, east and south.
rooms.10750: An iceberg floats here worn into a great round dome, smooth and white and pitted with hollows, so that from some angles it looks uncomfortably like a vast skull half sunk in the sea. Water drips from the brows of its empty eye sockets. The boat's wake slaps against it and echoes oddly. Beyond it, the sea is open all round.
rooms.10760: Seen through the haze, the iceberg here looks for a heartbeat like a tall ship under full sail, its pinnacles standing like masts and its flank like a white hull heeled over to the wind. Closer, it is only ice, groaning softly as it turns. Open water runs past it whichever way you turn.
rooms.10770: A pool of meltwater has gathered on the top of a squat iceberg here and spills over its rim in a little waterfall, a silver thread that falls the height of a tower and patters into the sea. The splash has worn a smooth hollow in the berg's flank. The ice shelf lies white and low not far off. Open water stretches away on every hand.
rooms.10780: A great slab has broken away from the ice shelf here, and the new face is raw and startlingly blue, sheer as a cut loaf, with water still streaming down it. The fallen piece floats a little way off as a new iceberg, rocking as it settles, and the sea between is choked with shattered ice. The shelf's edge runs on east and west, and north the floes drift in open water.
rooms.10779: From here you can see over the lip of the ice shelf to its top, a plain of snow as level as a frozen lake that runs on and on until it melts into the white sky. Wind sweeps loose snow off its edge in long, smoking plumes that drift down over the water. The shelf's cliff runs east and west, and north the sea lies open.
rooms.10769: A broad avenue of open water runs here between two enormous floes, dark and straight as a canal, and the floes' edges stand up on either hand like low white walls. The water in it is still, and the boat glides with barely a sound. Side leads branch off between the floes, so you may go on in any direction.
rooms.10759: Far off across the floes something breathes out with a long, booming whoosh, and a column of mist rises above the ice, hangs, and drifts apart in the wind. Then there is nothing but the slap of water and the creak of the floes. The sea around the boat is wide and empty, and the way lies open north, east, south and west.
rooms.10749: A hidden rock lies just under the surface here, and every so often the swell rears up over it, green and glassy, and breaks in a sudden burst of white that falls back hissing. Between breakers there is nothing to show it is there. North, the black skerry rises above the water; east, south and west, the sea is deep again.
rooms.10739: A low skerry of black rock rises from the sea here, glazed with ice and streaked with frozen spray, and on its crown squats a hut of piled stones roofed with whale jawbones and turf, a hunters' shelter against the worst of the weather. A smoke-stained hide hangs across its doorway. The swell creams around the rocks, and the boat rides in their lee. Open water lies all about the skerry.
rooms.10729: Two pillars of ice stand up from the sea here, all that remains of an arched iceberg whose span has fallen, and the wreckage of the arch still drifts between them in a raft of blue blocks. They lean a little farther apart each season. South, the black skerry shows low over the water, and the sea is open north, east and west as well.
rooms.10719: A small white sun hangs low over the sea here, round and hard as a silver coin and about as warm, and every floe throws a long blue shadow across the water. Your own breath hangs in front of your face. The stranded bergs glint in a line to the north, and the other ways lie open among the floes.
rooms.10709: A stranded berg is melting here, streaming from a hundred places at once, so that its face is hung with little waterfalls that splash and chuckle down into the sea. The water around it is fresh enough to taste and full of tumbling chips of ice. The grounded bergs run east and west from it, and south the sea lies open.
rooms.10708: The shoal that grounds the stranded bergs comes close to the surface here, and the boat's keel scrapes ominously over rocks furred with weed. Brown kelp streams in the current, and the swell steepens and breaks in odd places with no warning. The bergs tower beside you in their line, running east and west, and deeper water lies south.
rooms.10718: A forest of kelp grows up from the bottom here, its long brown fronds swaying just below the surface and its floats bobbing on top like strings of olives. The water among the weed is calm and smells of iodine and salt. North the stranded bergs stand on their shoal; elsewhere the kelp thins out into open sea.
rooms.10728: The water here is so clear that you can see straight down to the bottom, a long way below, where pale starfish and spiny urchins lie scattered over grey stones like dropped jewellery. Your boat seems to hang in the air above them. The cold rises off the water in a breath you can feel. All around, the sea stretches open.
rooms.10738: Freezing fog lies on the sea here, and wherever it touches it grows rime, long white feathers of frost that build up on the oars, the gunwale and your hood until the boat looks furred like a winter beast. Sound carries strangely; the swell on the skerry close to the east seems to come from everywhere at once. The open sea runs on unseen to the north, south and west.
rooms.10748: A hole has opened in the clouds overhead, and through it shows a hard, deep blue sky, so that one shaft of sunlight falls on the sea here and sets the nearest bergs blazing white. Outside that pool of light the world stays grey. It feels almost warm for a moment. Open water lies all around, every way you look.
rooms.10758: An iceberg rises here in the shape of a great crouching beast, its head low between its paws and its back humped, as if it were waiting for something to pass. Wind has polished its flanks to a glassy sheen. The boat's shadow slides across its feet. The sea runs open past it, north and south, east and west.
rooms.10768: A thin rind of new ice has formed here, hard and brittle as window glass, and the bow breaks it into long, ringing shards that skate away across the surface with a sound like tinkling bells. Behind the boat a black lane of water marks your passage. The ice shelf shows as a low white line beyond. Past the rind, the sea is open every way.
rooms.10778: The edge of the ice shelf has been undercut here into a long overhang, and from its lip hang icicles as long as spears, dripping steadily into the shadowed water beneath. Far back under the overhang the sea gurgles in the dark. It looks ready to fall at any moment. The shelf runs east and west, and north lies open water.
rooms.10777: An iron stake has been driven into the face of the ice shelf here, just above the waterline, its head rusted to a lump and a few strands of frayed rope still knotted around it, where some boat once moored against the ice. Above it the shelf rises in a sheer white cliff. The shelf's edge runs east and west, and north the floes drift on open water.
rooms.10767: Without warning a gust comes pouring down off the ice shelf here, bitter and heavy, flattening the sea into a hissing sheet of spray and shoving the boat sideways before dying as suddenly as it came. Then the water lies still again, ruffled and grey. The shelf glimmers a little way off. The way is open in every direction.
rooms.10757: A snow squall closes in here, driving thick and sideways, and in a moment the world is gone: no bergs, no floes, no sky, only whirling white and the grey water slapping at the bow. Ice crusts your eyebrows. When the squall thins, the open sea shows again all round, north and south, east and west.
rooms.10747: A bow of pale light arches over the mist here, white instead of coloured, a ghostly rainbow with its feet set somewhere out on the floes. It moves when the boat moves, always the same distance off. Beneath it the water is grey and gentle, and you may row on in any direction you please.
rooms.10737: An iceberg here has been pierced clean through by the sea, leaving a great arch tall enough for a ship to sail under, its roof hung with icicles and its inner walls glowing a deep, clear blue. Drips fall from the span in a steady patter. Rowing beneath it would be a fine thing, if you trusted it more. Open water runs on around the berg on every side.
rooms.10727: From here the edge of the pack ice can be seen to the west, a long white line of jammed floes that grinds and mutters without rest, and loose pieces broken from it come drifting past the boat one by one. The light is flat and grey, and the sea has no shine to it. North, south and east the water stays clear.
rooms.10717: Rafts of kelp torn loose by some storm drift here, great tangled mats of brown weed and floats knotted together, and they wrap around the oars and drag at the boat. Small shells and splinters of wood are caught up in them. East, the living kelp forest sways beneath the surface; north stand the stranded bergs, and south and west the water is clear.
rooms.10707: A stranded berg here has been carved by wind and wave into the likeness of a castle, with a squat keep, a crumbling curtain wall and a gate-arch filled solid with ice, and the swell boils white about its foot like a moat. Snow lies along its battlements. East and west the grounded bergs stand in their line, and south the open sea waits.
rooms.10706: A tunnel runs through the stranded berg before you, a blue-lit bore through the ice with a pale circle of daylight at its far end, but its throat is packed with brash and slush that heave with every swell, and no boat could pass. A cold wind breathes out of it. The line of bergs runs east and west, and south lies the open sea.
rooms.10716: Floes broken from the pack wander out across the water here, slow and heavy, thick slabs of old ice with snow drifted on their backs and green weed fringing their undersides. They jostle the boat with gentle, ponderous shoves. West, the pack itself lies white and close; the stranded bergs stand north, and open water runs east and south.
rooms.10726: Someone has built a cache on the floe here: a low cairn of stones, carried out from some far beach, heaped over whatever lies beneath, with the curved ribs of a seal poking out between them. A bone stake topped with a tuft of hide marks the spot. Other floes jostle around it, and the water is open on every side.
rooms.10736: The sun has sunk low behind the clouds, and a long, level light pours out beneath them, turning the pack ice to the west a soft gold and the nearby floes to rose and amber. Every ripple holds a spark. The cold sharpens as the light fades. Open water leads north, east and south, and west toward the glowing ice.
rooms.10746: The floes here are old and rotten, grey and honeycombed with holes, sagging into the sea under their own weight, and every so often one gives way with a soft, wet collapse into slush. The water around them is cloudy with crumbled ice. The pack groans not far off. Clearer water lies north, east, south and west.
rooms.10756: A black band runs through the iceberg here, a stripe of grit and ash laid down in some year when a mountain burned far away and its smoke fell on the snow, and the berg is clean white above and below it. The sea has worn the dark band into a deep groove. Open water lies around it every way.
rooms.10766: Not far off, the pack ice and the ice shelf grind together where they meet, and the noise of it fills the air: a ceaseless creaking and groaning, broken now and then by a crack like an oak splitting. A haze of powdered ice hangs over the meeting place. Open water still leads north, east, south and west, but the boat trembles with every crack.
rooms.10776: The edge of the ice shelf runs here into the pack ice, and the two have heaved each other up into a chaos of tilted blocks and shattered slabs, some standing on end like gravestones. Nothing could find a way through that. Open water lies back to the north; east the shelf's white cliff runs on, and west a last pocket of water lies hemmed in by the ice.
rooms.10775: This is a dead end of grey water, hemmed in where the pack ice and the ice shelf have frozen together into one white, broken wall. The ice here is silent, gripped so tight it cannot move, and the stillness weighs on you. The only ways out are north along the edge of the pack, or east beside the shelf.
rooms.10765: The pack ice ends here in a beach of slush and brash, a shifting margin of broken ice that rises and falls with the swell and sighs as it moves. Beyond it the pack runs out of sight, white and jagged. Open water runs north and south along its edge, and east toward the middle of the sea.
rooms.10755: A line of poles runs off across the pack here, each topped with a rag or a tuft of hide, marking the way hunters cross the ice in the deep of winter, though no one could walk it now, with the floes heaving and leads opening between them. The pack creaks and grumbles endlessly. Open water follows its edge north and south, and runs east into the sea.
rooms.10745: Fog lies over the pack ice here, so thick that the white of the ice and the white of the air run together, and the edge of the floes is only a grey line where the water stops. Out in the fog the pack cracks and shifts with sounds like slammed doors. The water runs north and south along the edge, and east, away from it.
rooms.10735: An iceberg has been caught in the pack ice here and frozen fast, standing up out of the jammed floes like a ship locked in harbour for the winter, its sides scoured by the grinding ice around it. The pack heaves against it with a deep, steady groaning. Clear water runs along the pack's edge north and south, and the open sea lies east.
rooms.10725: Along the edge of the pack ice the floes have been driven together into a pressure ridge, a wall of upended blocks taller than a man, glazed green at their broken edges and heaped with snow. Every so often the ridge shudders and a block crashes down. You can follow it north or south, or turn east into open water.
rooms.10715: The pack ice here is old ice, many years old, its floes worn into rolling hummocks like snowy hills, smooth and blue-white, with old meltpools frozen into glassy hollows between them. It lies quieter than the newer ice, heavy and sure of itself. The water runs north toward the stranded bergs, south along the pack, and east into the open sea.
rooms.10705: In this corner the stranded bergs and the pack ice have frozen into one another, making a single white wall that curves around the boat, and the water lies still and black in its shelter. Icicles hang from the overhangs, and the ice ticks and creaks as it settles. You can leave only east, along the line of bergs, or south beside the pack.

10799.description: The cairn is a squat pile of black stones as tall as two men, bristling with the bleached jawbones and ribs of whales. A pole on its top still flies a few grey rags that were once red, and the stones at its foot are scratched with tally marks and names too worn to read.

10537.description: Her timbers are blackened oak, bolted with iron that has bled long rusty tears down the wood. On a split board near the bow you can still make out a few painted letters: SEA WREN, OF PORT HALYON.

10590.description: Someone once shored this shaft with ship's timbers, and the timbers gave way under the weight of sand and stone. Through a gap between the fallen slabs you can glimpse the edge of a carved stone step, green with weed, before the dark swallows it.

10543.description: The boulder is a rounded lump of red granite, nothing like the black rock of the coast, scored across with long scratches where the glacier dragged it. Someone has daubed a crude eye on its side in tar, perhaps for luck, perhaps as a warning.

10562.keywords: boat ship's thwarts planks transom rope
10562.description: A name has been burned into her transom: WREN'S CHICK. A rusted iron ring is still set in her bow, and from it hangs a stump of frayed rope, cut clean through.

10787.description: Someone set these ribs into the shingle long ago and lashed them together at the top with sinew, now rotted to grey threads. Scratched into one rib are rows of tiny figures: boats, harpoons, seals, and a long, coiling shape that fills the bone from end to end.

10761.description: Peering close, you can make out a head as long as a boat, its jaws half open, and pale scales furred with frost along a body that coils back on itself again and again. Whether it is dead or only sleeping, there is no telling.

10739.description: Peering in past the hide, you see a hut barely big enough for three to lie down, its floor spread with old moss and its walls black with soot. A row of names has been scratched into the lintel stone, and beneath them, more freshly cut, someone has added: GONE TO THE BAY.

10755.description: The nearest pole is a whale's rib driven deep into the ice, hung with a strip of red-dyed hide and a little carved bone fish that clicks against it in the wind. The poles beyond it march away over the pack, each a little fainter, until the white swallows them.

creatures.long_desc: A grey seal lolls on a floe nearby, watching you with large, wet, dark eyes.
creatures.description: Its sleek coat is mottled grey and silver and still dripping, and its long, whiskered face looks almost like a sad old dog's. It is fat and clumsy on the ice, humping along on its belly, but in the water it turns and vanishes as quick as a fish. A pale scar runs across its back where something with teeth once nearly had it.

creatures.long_desc: A crested penguin stands on the edge of a floe, its yellow plumes ruffled by the wind.
creatures.description: It stands no higher than your knee, a plump little bird in black and white, with a pair of shaggy yellow plumes sprouting over its red eyes like eyebrows. It looks you up and down with grave suspicion and gives an indignant croak. Its stubby wings are as hard as paddles, and its hooked beak is sharp enough to draw blood.

creatures.long_desc: An ice crab scuttles sideways over the stones, its pale claws raised and clacking.
creatures.description: Its shell is the size of a buckler, ridged and blue-white like old sea ice, and frost clings to the joints of its long, spiny legs. One claw is swollen far bigger than the other and looks able to crack a man's shin. Small black eyes on stalks follow your every move.
rooms: The Quiet Bay beyond the Ice Wall

creatures.long_desc: A seal hunter sits in a narrow skin boat, harpoon raised, scanning the floes.
creatures.description: He is short and broad, his face burned dark by wind and glare, and he is wrapped from crown to boots in sealskin sewn with sinew. A harpoon with a head of carved bone rests across his knees, its line coiled neatly at his feet, and a charm of yellowed ivory hangs at his throat. He gives you a slow nod and goes back to watching the ice.

creatures.long_desc: A killer whale circles in the dark water, its tall black fin slicing through the swell.
creatures.description: It is longer than your boat, a sleek mass of glossy black with a white patch behind each eye and a white belly that flashes as it rolls. Its fin stands up from its back as tall as a man, and when it opens its jaws the teeth are as thick as tent pegs. It watches you with a cold, clever interest that is worse than hunger.

creatures.long_desc: A frost sea serpent rears out of the water, rime crackling along its coils.
creatures.description: Its coils are thicker than a barrel and sheathed in pale blue scales that glitter like ice, and frost smokes from its skin wherever the air touches it. A ragged crest of fins runs down its back, and its long head is armoured with bony plates, the jaws lined with glassy, needle-thin teeth. Where it breathes, the sea around it skins over with ice.

items.room_desc: A sealskin cloak lies here in a sleek grey heap.
items.description: A heavy cloak of grey sealskin, the fur turned outward to shed the spray and the seams sewn tight with sinew so that no wind finds its way through. It smells faintly of fish oil and smoke.

items.room_desc: A small charm of yellowed ivory lies here on a leather thong.
items.description: A piece of walrus tusk carved into a curled-up seal, worn smooth and yellow by years of handling and hung on a thong of plaited hide. The seal hunters say it keeps the sea from taking you, so long as you never take it off.

items.room_desc: A harpoon with a head of carved bone lies here.
items.description: A stout shaft of driftwood as long as a man, tipped with a barbed head of carved whalebone lashed on with sinew. A loop of line is knotted below the head, and the shaft is worn smooth where a hunter's hand has gripped it.

items.room_desc: A great curved tooth, creamy white, lies here.
items.description: A conical tooth as long as your palm and as thick as a thumb, creamy white and ringed with faint bands like the rings of a tree. Carvers and charm-makers prize them, and the seal hunters count one worth a whole season's catch.

items.room_desc: A pale blue pearl lies here, rimed with frost.
items.description: A pearl as big as a thrush's egg, pale blue and cold enough to sting the fingers, with a thin skin of frost that grows back as fast as you breathe it away. They are said to form only in the gullets of the frost sea serpents, and any jeweller brave enough to handle one will pay a small fortune for it.
